segments.heading: Segment 1
segments.text:
You woke up this morning, and before your feet touched the floor, your mind had already made a list. Not a list of what you have. A list of what is still missing.
The conversation you are dreading. The thing that has still not changed. And underneath it all, a quieter thought. I know I should be thankful. I just do not feel it today. And that feels like guilt.

So before the day asks anything of you, let us set that list down. Just for a few minutes. You can pick it up again later. Take one slow breath.
And instead of holding your hands closed, open them.

<#1#>

There is a line in the saddest book in the Bible.
Lamentations chapter three, verses twenty-two and twenty-three.
Because of the Lord's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
Notice the word new. Not leftover. Not what remained after yesterday used up its share.
New. Whatever you spent yesterday, this morning has its own supply, and it was here before you woke.

If mornings like this are hard for you, subscribe and pray with us. You were never meant to start them alone.

In the next few minutes, we are not asking God for one more thing.
We are asking him to open our eyes to mercy, grace, and the blessings that have been here the whole time. Wherever you are, let us come to him together.

<#1#>

His compassions never fail. They are new every morning.

Read it again slowly, because there are three quiet things hidden in that sentence.

The first is this. We are not consumed. It does not say we were never hurt. It does not say nothing broke. It says we were not finished off. Something held.
Something carried us through a year we did not think we could carry. That is not luck, and it is not our own strength.

The second is this. His compassions never fail. Mercy does not thin out because it has been asked for too often.
There is no register in heaven where our name has appeared too many times. Nothing about us has ever worn you down, and nothing about us ever will.

And the third is the one we need most this morning. New every morning. Not warmed over. Not the portion left from yesterday.
God did not hand us the remainder of what we failed to use. He opened something fresh while we were still asleep and unaware of it.

Lord, we have heard these words before. Many of us have read them on a wall, or on a card, or at the beginning of a hard year.
Help us hear them this morning as if they were written for today. Not as a beautiful sentence. As something true about the room we are sitting in right now.

We are not going to rush past that. Before we ask you for anything, we want to stay here a moment longer and simply agree with it. Your love held us. Your compassion did not fail.
And this morning arrived already carrying what it needed. Which means the first thing worth saying is not a request. It is a thank you.

<#1#>

Look at the light in the room. It arrived without being asked. Nobody negotiated for it. Nobody earned it.
It simply came, the way it has come every day of your life, and most of those days you did not thank anyone for it.
And it will be gone again tonight, and tomorrow it will come back, and you will not have asked for anything in return.

Psalm chapter one hundred three, verse two says,
Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
Notice who is being spoken to there. Not God. Not other people.
The writer is talking to his own soul, because he knows it will not do this on its own. Gratitude is not a feeling that shows up.
It is a direction we have to turn ourselves toward, sometimes firmly. The way you would gently turn a child's face toward you so they can hear you. So this morning we are turning.
Not because our hearts are full, but because you are worthy whether they are full or not.

Heavenly Father, thank you for last night. Not for anything dramatic. For the ordinary fact that we lay down and lost consciousness for hours, and you did not. You do not sleep.
So while we were unaware, unable to manage anything, unable to fix a single situation we had been worrying about all day, you kept watch.
Thank you for the hours we cannot account for. Thank you that our worrying stopped and your working did not. We did not hold the world together while we slept. You did.
And we woke to a morning we did not build.

And thank you for the things that never happened. The accident we did not have. The phone call that did not come.
We will never know what you kept away from us, because you did it quietly and did not tell us. We have spent years thanking you only for what arrived. Thank you for what never reached us.

And thank you for something we almost never say out loud. Thank you for who you are, apart from anything you have done for us.
If you had never answered a single prayer of ours, you would still be good. If nothing in our circumstances ever improves, you would still be faithful.
We are so used to measuring you by our results that we forget you existed in perfect goodness before we needed anything. You are not kind because we are useful.
You are kind because that is your nature.

And before we say anything else, thank you for the cross.
Everything we are about to pray this morning rests on a debt we could not pay and did not pay. Mercy is not a mood you are in. It cost you something.
Let it never become ordinary to us that you came down.

And yet, Father, if we are honest with you this morning, that is exactly what has happened.

<#1#>

How many mornings have we been given, and how many did we actually receive?

Father, we have to say something honest before we go any further. We have become people who are handed something extraordinary every single day and barely look up.

We ate meals this week we cannot remember eating. We stood in a hot shower and thought about a problem the whole time.
We drove a familiar road and arrived without remembering the drive. Someone spoke to us and we were physically present and completely absent.
We counted what was missing before we counted anything we had, and we did it so automatically that it did not even feel like a choice.

Forgive us. Not in a general way. Forgive us specifically, for the ingratitude we would never admit to anyone, because it does not look like sin. It looks like being busy.

And Lord, there is a second thing, and it is heavier.

Some of us feel guilty for not feeling grateful. We have tried to work up the emotion. We have told ourselves how much worse it could be.
And the numbness did not move, and now we are ashamed of our own hearts on top of everything else. It is a strange kind of loneliness.

Hear this. Your mercy did not arrive because we felt something. It was already new before we woke, before we had a single feeling about you at all.
You do not wait at a distance until our hearts warm up.
Because of your great love we are not consumed, and that was true this morning while we were still cold.

<#1#>

So we are putting something down.

Not our future. Not our people. Not the list. Just one thing.

We are putting down the weight of having to hold all of it ourselves.
The quiet belief that if we stop managing, calculating and bracing for one moment, everything will come apart.
We have carried that so long we stopped noticing its weight, the way you stop noticing a bag you have worn all day until you finally set it down.

We are setting it down now.

We are not asking you to remove anything yet. We are simply admitting we are not the ones holding this together, and we never were.

And into that honesty, Father, your mercy comes. It does not wait for us to be better first.

<#1#>

Mercy does not run out.

Say it again, because most of us do not actually believe it. Mercy does not run out.

Father, there is a particular kind of tiredness that comes from failing at the same thing more than once. It is not the failure itself. It is the repetition.
The first time we came to you about it, we were broken. The tenth time, we were embarrassed.
And somewhere after that we stopped bringing it at all, because we could not stand the sound of our own voice asking again.

Some of us lost our temper with our children again this week. The same tone. The same regret afterward, standing in the hallway.
Some of us broke a promise we made to ourselves in this very chair, at this very hour, not long ago.
Some of us are carrying something nobody in our life knows about, and the worst part is not the thing itself.
The worst part is that we know exactly how many times we have done it.

And into that, your word says your compassions never fail.

Never fail. Not they last a long time. Not they stretch further than most. They do not fail. There is no number at which they stop.
We have been quietly assuming mercy works like patience, and that we have been drawing down a supply that must be nearly gone by now. That is not what you said. You said new. Every morning.
Which means the mercy available to us this morning has never been touched, because it did not exist yesterday.

This is the difference between mercy and endurance. Endurance wears thin.
It is a finite thing being stretched, and everyone who has ever loved a difficult person knows the feeling of it running low. Your compassion is not being stretched. It is being renewed.
Nothing in you is being used up by us.

So we come. Not with a better argument than last time.
Not with a promise to do better, because we have offered those before and you were not impressed by them then either.

We come the only way anyone has ever come to you. Empty-handed, and welcome anyway.

And we can say that for one reason only. Not because we are sorry enough, but because Jesus already carried it.
It was already settled at the cross long before this morning. Mercy is not you overlooking what we did. It is you having paid for it.

Meet us here. Not at the version of us we are hoping to become. Here, at the version that failed again.

And Father, do something further. Whatever mercy we receive this morning, let it not stop with us.
There is someone we will see today who has failed us in a way we have not released. Give us enough of your mercy that we can spare some.
Let us be as slow with them as you have been with us.

But mercy is not the whole of it. Mercy keeps us from being consumed. Mercy deals with what is behind us.
And in a few hours we will be standing in front of something we do not have the strength for. For that, we need something else.

<#1#>

There is something on today's schedule that we are not strong enough for.

Most of us know exactly what it is. We knew before we opened our eyes. A conversation we have rehearsed four times and still cannot start.
A room we have to walk into where we are the only one who will say the hard thing. A drive we have to make alone.
A person at home who needs another day of care from us, and we gave everything we had yesterday.

Or it is nothing dramatic at all.
It is the same work, the same hours, the same tasks we have done a thousand times, and somewhere along the way we stopped being able to find the point of it.

Second Corinthians chapter twelve, verse nine.
My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.

Father, we want to be careful with that verse, because Paul did not write it after you fixed his problem.
He asked you three times to take something away, and you did not take it away.
What he received instead was you, in the middle of it, and he called that better.

So we are not going to ask for an easier day. We are asking for grace to be sufficient for the day we actually have.

And we notice the word you chose. Sufficient. Not abundant. Not overflowing. Enough. Grace usually arrives at the exact size of the next step and not one inch further. That is uncomfortable for people like us.
We would rather see the whole staircase before we move. But it means we will never be handed more than we need and left to manage it alone.
It means the strength for eleven o'clock will be there at eleven o'clock, and not at seven. That is not you withholding. That is you keeping us close.

So give us grace that is still patient by the afternoon, not only in the first quiet hour of the day.
Make us kind when we are depleted, because anyone can be kind when they are rested.
Hold us to a promise we made back when we had more energy than we have now.
And let us do ordinary work faithfully when nobody notices and nothing about it feels significant.

And where we are weakest today, do not make us strong. Make yourself evident. Let somebody see something in us that we know is not ours.

And if we fail at it anyway. If we hear ourselves saying the thing we swore we would not say. Do not let us decide that the morning was wasted. Your grace was still sufficient.
We just met the end of ours first.

But there is one more thing.
We keep asking you for strength to face what is coming, and we have not once stopped to notice what is already in our hands.

<#1#>

There is a glass of water within reach of most of us right now.

We poured it without a thought. Clean and safe, in the amount we wanted, at the temperature we wanted.
It arrives through a wall in our home whenever we ask for it.
For most of human history, and for a great many people alive this morning, that single glass would have been the most valuable object in the room.

Father, we did not see it.

James chapter one, verse seventeen says every good and perfect gift is from above. Every one. Not the rare ones.
Not the ones that arrive after long prayer and finally make us cry.
Every good thing in our lives came down from you, including the ones so constant that we stopped registering them as gifts at all.

This is our real request this morning, and it is the one we came for.

Open our eyes.

Not to something new. To what is already here.

Let us hear it right now, before we go anywhere. Somewhere in this house there is the sound of another person moving. We are not alone in the world.
Our body is breathing without being told to, and it has done that our whole lives without a single instruction from us.
There is a key in our pocket, and a door somewhere that opens for us.
There is a name in our phone we could call at a bad hour and they would answer.
There is food in the kitchen that we did not worry about yesterday. There is a pair of shoes that fit us, and somewhere to be today.

Some of us are praying beside someone we once begged you for. We asked for them for years.
They are here, in the next room, and we have not thanked you for them in months.

We have been treating all of that as the background. As the setting the story happens in. It is not the setting, Father. It is the story.
It is you, providing, continuously, in a way so steady that it became invisible.

And forgive us for what we have made the word blessing mean. We have made it mean the thing we do not have yet. The answer that is still coming.
We have been standing in the middle of an answered prayer we prayed five years ago, complaining about a different one.

We are not asking for more this morning. We are asking for sight. Give us eyes for what is already here.
Let us walk through this ordinary day and keep catching ourselves noticing, not because any of it is impressive, but because all of it is yours.

And when we start seeing it, do not let us hold it.
Because we are not the only ones in this house, on this street, or in this hour who need something from you.

<#1#>

Somewhere this morning, someone is awake and cannot find one single thing to be thankful for.

They are not being difficult. They have looked. Father, we are praying for them now.
Not that their situation would suddenly reverse, but that before this day is over you would give them one thing. One. Small enough to be believable. A stranger who is kind for no reason.
A few minutes where the pressure lifts. Something ordinary that lands like it was placed there on purpose.
Give them a single crack of light, and give them the ability to see it when it comes, because the seeing is the harder half. We know. We were there.

And Father, we bring you the ones who have been waiting a long time.

They have prayed the same prayer so many times that the words have gone flat in their mouth. The answer has not come, and worse, no explanation has come either.
We are not going to pretend to know your timing, and we are not going to hand them a slogan this morning.
But we ask you for something specific for them. Give them the ability to be thankful while they are still waiting, which is the hardest gratitude there is. Not thankful for the delay. Thankful in it.
Let them find you good before they find you finished.

There is another group, and we hold them gently.

Some who hear this have lost someone.
And a strange guilt has attached itself to them, because there are moments in the day when they laugh, or enjoy the sun, or forget for an hour, and then it feels like a betrayal.
Father, tell them it is not. Gratitude is not disloyalty to grief. They can hold both.
You are near to the brokenhearted, and you are not standing over them waiting for them to cheer up. Sit with them this morning.
Let them weep and let them be thankful in the same hour, and let neither one cancel the other.

And there are the ones who are keeping someone else alive this morning. A parent. A husband. A daughter who moved back home.
They get up before they are ready, every day, and nobody claps. Father, they have been giving from a place that has nothing left in it. Carry the part of it they cannot carry.
And let somebody thank them today in a way they can actually hear.

And last, our own homes.

The people we live with have become the most familiar thing in our lives, which is exactly why we stopped seeing them. Forgive us.
Let gratitude be spoken out loud in our houses today, not only felt.
Let us tell one person specifically what we are glad for about them, and not in general terms.
Make our home a place where good things get named instead of assumed.

And now, Father, bring all of this back to us. Because everything we have just asked for other people is something we have to choose for ourselves first.

<#1#>

I want to stop saying we for a moment, and speak only for myself.

I choose to count what I have been given before I count what I am missing. That list was there when I woke up. It is still there.
Nothing on it has been solved while we have been praying.
But it is no longer the first thing I see, and I am not handing it the first hour of my day again.
I choose to walk into today as someone who has already received more than I asked for, rather than someone still waiting to be paid.

And I will thank you today even if today changes nothing.

That is the harder one. If the phone does not ring. If the answer does not come.
If this evening looks exactly like last evening and the thing I have been carrying is still sitting there at the end of it, I will still say that your mercy was new this morning, because it was.
My gratitude is not a receipt for services rendered. I am not thankful because the situation improved.
I am thankful because you are who you said you are, and that was settled long before my circumstances got involved.

And then there is this, and it is the thing I most want to say.

Lord, I have spent a long time wanting things from you. Mercy, so I can be clean. Grace, so I can be strong. Blessings, so my life can be full.
All of that is good, and you offer all of it freely.

But this morning I want you.

More than mercy. More than grace. More than every good thing that comes down from you. I want the One they come from. Not the gifts arriving from your hand. Your face.
Because it is entirely possible to love what God provides and slowly stop loving God.
I do not want to find out one day that I have been in love with the provision all along.

I have prayed to you for years the way I would text someone I only contact when I need something. I am not proud of that.
I do not know how to fix it in one morning.
But I want to want you, and I am saying it plainly, in case wanting to want you is where it starts.

If I had everything I have prayed for and did not have you, I would have nothing.

If I have you and nothing else ever changes, I have enough.

And I can only say any of this because you chose me first, on a morning when I was not looking for you at all.

So take this day. It is not much, and it is not particularly impressive, but it is all of it. I choose you.
This morning, and at eleven o'clock when it is harder, and tonight when nobody is watching. I choose you.

<#1#>

Because of the Lord's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

That was true before we prayed. It will still be true tomorrow, when we have forgotten it again.

The list is still there. We are not pretending otherwise. But we picked up something else first this morning, and we are carrying that out the door with us.
That we were held through a night we did not manage. That we were met with mercy we had already used many times.
That grace will arrive at exactly the size of the next step. And that we have been surrounded the whole time by good things we had stopped seeing.

Nothing in our circumstances has changed in the last half hour. Something in our eyes has.

We will forget this by lunch. That is alright. Forgetting is not failing.
We will come back tomorrow and let it be new again, because that is the one thing it is guaranteed to be.

We choose to walk into this day as people who have already received, not people still waiting to begin.

<#1#>

Father, send us out.

May mercy reach you before the news does today. May grace be enough for you in the exact place you already know you are not enough.
And may your eyes keep opening, again and again, to what has been in front of you the whole time.
May you become someone who notices, and who says it out loud. May you be hard to discourage, because you have learned to count what is already in your hands.

In the name of Jesus we pray.
Amen.

Before you go, one small thing. Type one word in the comments. One thing you are thankful for this morning. Just one word.
Then read a few of the others, because someone down there is going to need to borrow yours today.

If this helped you start the morning differently, send it to the person you thought of when we prayed for those who could not find anything to be thankful for.
Leaving a like helps this prayer reach someone waking up alone with their list.
And if you want to keep beginning your days like this, subscribe, and we will meet you here tomorrow.

One last thing. Gratitude is not meant to keep us in the room. It sends us out the door.
And the day waiting on the other side of that door has things in it we cannot see yet, and cannot carry on our own.
That is the next prayer, and it is already on your screen. It will be waiting for you whenever you are ready.
